chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Bukeyr, from al-Halabi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why was kissing the Stone prescribed?' He said: 'When God, Mighty and Majestic, took the covenant of the Children of Adam, He summoned the Stone from Paradise and commanded it, so it swallowed the covenant. Thus, it testifies for those who fulfill their covenant with it.'

key_terms.اسْتِلَام: Touching or kissing the Black Stone — a sunnah act during tawaf (circumambulation) of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْحَجَر: The Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) — a sacred stone embedded in the corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمُوَافَاة: Faithfulness/fulfillment — being loyal to the covenant of wilayah (guardianship)
key_terms.مِيثَاق: The covenant — specifically the pre-eternal covenant (mithaq al-dharr) when souls affirmed God's Lordship and the authority of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Why is kissing the Black Stone prescribed in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Al-Halabi, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), asked why kissing the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) was prescribed as part of hajj. The Imam explained that the Black Stone originated in Paradise and was charged by God to receive and preserve the primordial covenant (mithaq) taken from all of humanity before creation. By kissing or touching the Stone during hajj, a believer affirms their loyalty to this covenant, and the Stone will testify on their behalf on the Day of Judgment. This hadith connects the ritual of istilam to the foundational theological concept of the pre-eternal covenant of wilayah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Al Halby who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why was kissing the (Black) Stone made to be?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Took the Covenant of the Children of Adam<sup>as</sup>, Called the (Black) Stone from the Paradise, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Commanded it and it devoured the Covenant. Thus, it would testify for the ones who were loyal to it with the loyalty (to the Wilayah)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Why should one touch (kiss) the Stone?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, made a covenant with the children of Adam, He called the Stone from paradise and gave it a command. It swallowed up (fed it to itself) the covenant and it will testify in favor of those who comply with safe return of the trust.’”
